chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Idris ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him and said, 'May I be your ransom, we have farms (diya'), and they have boundaries containing grazing lands (mara'i). One of us has sheep and camels that need those grazing lands for their camels and sheep. Is it permissible for him to enclose (hima) the grazing land for his need of it?' He said, 'If the land is his land, then he may enclose it, and that enclosure extends to what he needs.'
He said, and I said to him, 'The man sells the grazing land?' He said, 'If the land is his land, there is no objection.'

key_terms.يَحْمِيَ: To enclose or designate as a protected area (hima)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on enclosing and selling grazing land owned by an individual?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of private property rights over grazing lands (*mara'i*) when they are attached to owned farmland (*diya'*), permitting both enclosure (*hima*) for specific utility and sale. It reflects the Shia juristic view that ownership extends to the necessary appurtenances of the land, resolving potential conflicts between individual utility and communal access by anchoring rights in clear title.
